Subject: Performance acceptance & MAP — initial ask

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement and our infra team asked for a concrete Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that captures the performance acceptance criteria for our chat use case (TTFT + streaming latencies across p50/p95/p99, throughput at target concurrency, and brief test harness/methodology).

High level constraints from our side:
- Typical seq length: ~512 tokens (avg 380)
- Target concurrency during peak: 24 concurrent chat sessions
- We expect first-token TTFT to be low for good UX; want to see both TTFT (first token) and streaming tail metrics per token.
- Will need test artifacts to validate in our staging VPC and audit the results.

Can you put together a short MAP with the evaluation plan and a close timeline? Procurement is pushing for a decision by end of May.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Khatri
Head of Product
Windward Health

Subject: Re: Performance acceptance & MAP — initial ask

Samir — appreciate the clarity. Draft MAP and evaluation plan attached (windward-qa.pdf). Below is a concise plan we propose so your team can evaluate and we can commit to a close timeline.

Summary acceptance gates (proposed):
1) Baseline assessment (week 1): Redwood runs a controlled baseline in our sandbox using your representative prompt set and model variant. Deliverable: baseline-ttft-report.csv with p50/p95/p99 TTFT and per-token streaming latency.
2) Windward validation (week 2): Windward runs the provided harness in your staging VPC (we provide container + instructions). Deliverable: staging run results and a short gap analysis.
3) Canary (week 3–4): Canary rollout on a subset of traffic (10%) for 72 hours to validate production behavior.
4) Decision gate (end of week 5): Accept / request remediation / decline.

Proposed numeric targets (for acceptance — adjustable based on your SLAs):
- First-token TTFT (512 token context, model: open-llm-v2-13B quantized): p50 <= 140ms, p95 <= 480ms, p99 <= 920ms
- Streaming per-token latency (tokens after first, measured as time between token emit events): p50 <= 25ms, p95 <= 75ms, p99 <= 140ms
- Sustained throughput at concurrency 24: median requests/sec per GPU consistent with expected scaling; we’ll provide cluster sizing guidance.
- Error rate: <0.5% end-to-end transient failures during test window.

Evaluation methodology high level:
- Harness: replayable load generator that mimics your conversation starter + user turn distribution. We provide config and seed corpus.
- Measurement: telemetry will capture TTFT (server timestamp of first token generation), per-token emit timestamps, queueing latency, and CPU/GPU utilization.
- Environment: two passes — Redwood sandbox (our infra) for baseline, and your staging VPC for reproducibility.
- Reproducibility: we’ll hand over the harness + Docker image + test corpus.

Owners & rough timeline:
- Redwood owner (bench execution + report): hannah_schmitt — kickoff Apr 24; baseline report Apr 27.
- Windward owner (staging run): Samir / infra — staging execution Apr 30–May 3.
- Contract/Procurement checkpoints: procurement team gets a week to review after Decision gate.

Questions for you (quick):
- Which model variant do you prefer as the primary baseline (13B vs 34B; fp16 vs quantized)?
- Any hard constraints on p99 that would be a non-starter?

I’ve attached the draft MAP (windward-qa.pdf) which includes a timeline graphic, test harness links, and acceptance checklist. Marcus and Lauren — looped for capacity and commercial notes.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks Hannah — this looks good and detailed, appreciate the clear gates. A few clarifying points before we lock schedules: 

1) Model variant: we'd like the baseline run on the 13B quantized variant, and one quick check on the 34B fp16 to understand headroom. Will that be possible?
2) Environment: can Redwood run the baseline in our staging VPC (we're fine with a short-lived test agent) or do you prefer to run an initial baseline in your sandbox and then replicate in our VPC? Ideally we'd like a Redwood-run baseline in our environment for closer parity.
3) Concurrency: our peak is 24 but we plan to test up to 32 concurrent sessions for safety margins. Please include both 24 and 32 in the throughput sweep.

If Redwood can run a baseline in our staging between Apr 24–28 that would be ideal. Procurement: please confirm any calendar constraints for the decision window.

Also please add an item to the MAP for regression monitoring after rollout (basic telemetry retention for two weeks).

Samir

Deliverables we will hand over after baseline:
- baseline-ttft-report.csv (attached) — raw timestamps and aggregated metrics
